html:
A Central Asian empire founded by Khitan refugees from China, ruling from Balasagun in what is now Kyrgyzstan between 1124 and 1218. Chinese histories call it the Western Liao. The map shows it in 1200.

When the Jurchen destroyed the Liao dynasty in 1125, the Liao prince Yelü Dashi led a band west. He took over the eastern Kara-Khanid lands and in 1141 crushed the Seljuk sultan Sanjar at Qatwan near Samarkand, making Transoxiana and Khwarazm his vassals. News of a non-Muslim king beating a Muslim army may have fed the European legend of Prester John.

The ruling Khitans were mostly Buddhist and used Chinese titles and ways of government, yet they left their Muslim subjects largely alone, taking tribute through local princes. In 1211 the Naiman prince Kuchlug, fleeing Genghis Khan, seized the throne. The Mongols killed him and took the realm in 1218, which put them on the border of the Khwarazmian Empire.
